claims.text: Differences in deformation and failure behavior between equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni and its quaternary and ternary subsets are caused by differences in local chemical short-range order.
The presence of all five elements in the quinary alloy promotes specific local atomic clustering.
The proposed clustering modifies local lattice distortion and dislocation interactions.
The proposed clustering gives the quinary alloy enhanced strain hardening and more gradual failure relative to lower-component subsets.
The quinary and compared equiatomic quaternary and ternary alloys are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
The controlled comparison should use identical processing and deformation-test conditions for the quinary, quaternary, and ternary alloys.
Comparable grain size, strain rate, environment, and thermomechanical processing are required to limit macrostructural confounding.
Chemically specific SRO clusters produce heterogeneous local lattice distortions.
These local distortions influence dislocation mobility and slip-system activation.
SRO clusters in the quinary alloy act as dislocation-pinning sites that increase the stress required for dislocation motion.
The increased resistance to dislocation motion raises strain hardening and delays plastic instability in the quinary alloy.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower yield strength.
Relative to the quinary baseline, the quaternary and ternary alloys will have lower strain-hardening capacity, earlier plastic instability, and more rapid failure.
The proposed relationship is restricted to similarly processed, single-phase FCC alloys tested at room temperature with comparable microstructures.
Changes in stacking-fault energy may also contribute to the observed mechanical-property differences.

The SRO hypothesis would be falsified if SRO does not differ significantly among the alloys or if measured SRO differences do not correlate with yield strength and strain-hardening rate under controlled conditions.
